q: What plug sockets are used in Bosnia and Herzegovina?
a: Bosnia and Herzegovina uses the same sockets as most EU countries, types C and F (Schuko), with two round pins. Chargers and devices from Croatia, Germany, Austria or Slovenia work without an adapter. Visitors from the UK, the USA or Switzerland need an adapter.

q: What is the voltage in Bosnia?
a: The voltage in Bosnia and Herzegovina is 230 V at 50 Hz, the same as in the EU. Devices from Europe work without a converter. If you are coming from the USA or Canada, check that your device supports 230 V, which most phone and laptop chargers do.

q: Do I need a plug adapter for Bosnia from the UK?
a: Yes, visitors from the UK and Ireland need an adapter, as Bosnia uses type C and F sockets at 230 V. Visitors from the USA, Switzerland and Australia need one too, while those from continental Europe do not. The simplest option is to bring a universal travel adapter. In most apartments the sockets are in the usual places, by the bed and in the kitchen.

q: Do apartments in Bihać have Wi-Fi?
a: Most accommodation in Bihać has free Wi-Fi, and so do most properties on apartmanibihac.com. In the houses by the Una the internet may be somewhat slower than in the town centre. If the internet is important for work, mention it in your enquiry and the owner will confirm what the connection is like.

q: Can I work remotely from Bihać?
a: Yes, Bihać is suitable for remote work, as the town has good mobile coverage and fast internet in most accommodation and cafés. For a stable connection it is better to stay in an apartment in the centre. You can check the internet speed at a specific property by enquiry on apartmanibihac.com.

q: How good is mobile coverage in Bihać?
a: Mobile coverage in Bihać is good, and all three major operators, BH Telecom, m:tel and HT Eronet, offer 4G, with faster internet in some places. In the Una canyon and in more remote villages the signal can be weaker. Foreign SIM cards work on roaming, but Bosnia is not in the EU roaming zone.

q: Will my EU phone work in Bosnia?
a: Yes, an EU phone works in Bosnia on roaming, but Bosnia is not part of the EU roam-like-at-home zone. Calls and data may be charged separately, sometimes at high rates. Before you travel, check the prices with your provider or buy a local SIM or eSIM.

q: What are shop opening hours in Bihać?
a: Supermarkets in Bihać usually open from early morning until the evening, roughly from 7 am to 9 or 10 pm, while smaller shops have shorter hours. On Saturdays most shops keep weekday hours, while on Sundays most shops in the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina are closed. Check the exact opening hours of a particular shop on Google Maps.

q: Are shops open on Sundays in Bihać?
a: Since November 2024 most shops in the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, including Bihać, have been closed on Sundays. Petrol stations, bakeries, florists, souvenir shops and shops at bus stations are open on Sundays. So do your main shopping on Saturday. Cafés and restaurants are also open on Sundays.

q: Where can I buy food on a Sunday in Bihać?
a: On Sundays you can buy basics at petrol stations and bakeries, which are allowed to open. Restaurants and cafés open as usual on Sundays. If you are arriving on a Sunday, it is best to buy groceries on the way or on Saturday before you arrive. Some small roadside producers also sell homemade products.

q: Are pharmacies open on Sundays in Bihać?
a: On Sundays and public holidays, an on-duty pharmacy is open in Bihać according to a rota. The rota is usually posted on pharmacy doors or published on local news websites. In an emergency the ambulance is always available on 124. Bring any regular medication from home.

q: What are the public holidays in Bosnia and Herzegovina?
a: The main public holidays in the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina are New Year (1 and 2 January), Independence Day (1 March), Labour Day (1 and 2 May) and Statehood Day (25 November). Religious holidays are also days off: both Bajrams (Eids), Catholic and Orthodox Easter, and Christmas. On these days many shops and offices are closed.

q: When is Bajram (Eid) in Bosnia?
a: Ramazanski Bajram (Eid al-Fitr) and Kurban Bajram (Eid al-Adha) are public holidays in the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and their dates move every year as they follow the Islamic lunar calendar. In 2026 Ramazanski Bajram fell on 20 and 21 March and Kurban Bajram on 27 and 28 May. On those days many shops are closed, while restaurants and cafés are mostly open.

q: Are shops open on public holidays in Bihać?
a: On major holidays such as New Year, Bajram and Christmas, many shops and offices in Bihać are closed or open for shorter hours. Restaurants, cafés and petrol stations are usually open. If you are arriving over a holiday, buy groceries the day before. Cafés by the Una and in the centre are usually open.

q: What language is spoken in Bihać?
a: Bosnian is spoken in Bihać; it is very close to Croatian and Serbian, so visitors from the region understand each other easily. The Latin alphabet is used. Many people, especially the young, speak English, and quite a few also speak German. Signs in town and on the roads are in the Latin alphabet, so it is easy to find your way around.

q: Do people in Bihać speak English?
a: Most younger people in Bihać speak good English, and communicating in English in tourism, restaurants and banks is usually not a problem. Older people speak English less often. We speak Bosnian, English and German, so feel free to contact us on +387 61 591 320.

q: Do people in Bihać speak German?
a: Yes, many people in Bihać speak at least some German, as many families have relatives in Germany, Austria and Switzerland. In summer the town is also visited by many members of the diaspora. We speak German and are happy to help you with bookings and information. You can also get by in German in many shops and cafés.

q: How do you say hello in Bosnian?
a: The most common greetings are "Dobar dan" (good day), "Dobro jutro" (good morning) and "Dobro veče" (good evening), and among friends "Zdravo" or "Ćao". "Thank you" is "Hvala", and "please" is "Molim". Some people also greet with "Selam" or "Selam alejkum", to which the reply is "Alejkum selam".

q: What are some useful Bosnian words for tourists?
a: Useful words are "hvala" (thank you), "molim" (please), "izvinite" (excuse me), "koliko košta" (how much is it), "račun, molim" (the bill, please), "voda" (water) and "kafa" (coffee). Locals appreciate it when a foreigner says at least "hvala" or "dobar dan" in their language. When you order, people will often reply in English or German if they notice you are a foreigner.

q: What time zone is Bihać in?
a: Bihać is in the Central European Time zone (CET, UTC+1), like Croatia, Germany and Austria. In summer the clocks go forward to summer time (CEST, UTC+2) on the same day as in the EU. Coming from Croatia, you do not need to change your watch. Your phone will adjust the time automatically anyway.

q: Is there a time difference between Croatia and Bosnia?
a: No, Croatia and Bosnia and Herzegovina are in the same time zone and change to summer time on the same day. When you cross the border at Izačić, the time stays the same. The same applies to Slovenia, Austria and Germany. Border crossing and bus timetables use the same time.

q: Where can I park in the centre of Bihać?
a: There are public car parks and on-street parking in the centre of Bihać, and some spaces in the inner centre are paid. In summer it is harder to find parking in the centre, especially in the evening. Ask in your enquiry on apartmanibihac.com whether the apartment has its own parking space, and the owner will also tell you where it is easiest to park.

q: How do I pay for parking in Bihać?
a: Check payment methods and prices on the sign at the car park itself, which shows the zone, the price and the hours when charges apply. At some car parks an attendant or a machine takes payment, and in some places you can pay by SMS from a local number. SMS payment often does not work with an EU number, so keep some small change in marks.

q: Do apartments in Bihać have parking?
a: It depends on the property: houses and holiday homes by the Una usually have space for a car next to the house, while in the centre it varies. For each property on apartmanibihac.com, the owner confirms parking in the reply to your enquiry. If you are coming with two cars or a van, mention it in advance.

q: Where can I get petrol in Bihać?
a: There are plenty of petrol stations on the main roads in and around Bihać, and most are open every day, including Sundays. You can pay by card or in cash, and euros are often accepted. There are no petrol stations in remote villages or in Una National Park, so fill up in town.

q: What types of fuel are available in Bosnia?
a: Petrol stations in Bosnia sell unleaded 95 and 98, diesel and usually autogas (LPG). Prices change almost weekly and vary between stations, so check them before your trip or at the pump. Fill up in Bihać if you are heading to Una National Park, as there are no petrol stations in the park.

q: Are there EV charging stations in Bihać?
a: There are several electric car charging points in Bihać, but the network is sparser than in Croatia or Western Europe. Check locations and availability in charging apps before you travel. Also ask your host whether you can charge your car from an ordinary socket at the property.

q: Where is the post office in Bihać?
a: The main post office is in the centre of Bihać, and there are smaller post offices in other parts of town. Postal services in this part of Bosnia are provided by BH Pošta. Check opening hours on the BH Pošta website or Google Maps, as post offices open shorter hours or close on Saturdays and public holidays.

q: Can I send a postcard from Bihać?
a: Yes, you can buy postcards and stamps at the post office, and postcards also at souvenir shops and kiosks. Hand in letters and postcards at the post office or drop them in a postbox. Post to EU countries usually takes from a few days to two weeks. For parcels and registered post, ask at the counter about prices and delivery times.

q: Where can I do laundry in Bihać?
a: Some apartments and houses have a washing machine, which you can check in the property description or in your enquiry on apartmanibihac.com. There are also dry cleaners and laundries in town. Self-service launderettes like those in Western Europe are rare, so do not rely on them.

q: Do the apartments have a washing machine?
a: It depends on the property: some apartments and most of the larger houses by the Una have a washing machine, while some smaller apartments do not. For a longer stay or a trip with children, mention in your enquiry that you need a washing machine. The owner will confirm what the property has before you book.

q: Is there food delivery in Bihać?
a: Yes, many restaurants and pizzerias in Bihać have their own delivery service, usually ordered by phone or via local apps and social media. Glovo stopped operating in Bosnia in mid-August 2026, so do not count on it. Your host can usually recommend places that deliver to your accommodation.

q: Can I get food delivered to a holiday house on the Una?
a: Delivery to holiday houses outside town, for example in Grmuša, depends on the restaurant and the distance. Some restaurants also deliver to surrounding villages, while others only deliver in town. Ask your host for reliable numbers; in Grmuša the Una Olympic Rafting restaurant by the river is also handy.

q: Do I need a passport or ID card to enter Bosnia?
a: EU citizens, including those from Croatia, Germany and Austria, can enter Bosnia with a valid ID card or passport. Citizens of some other countries need a passport, and some also need a visa. Check the requirements for your nationality on the website of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Children need their own travel document.

q: Do I need a green card for my car in Bosnia?
a: With an EU-registered car, check whether your insurance covers Bosnia and Herzegovina, as Bosnia is not in the EU. The green card must show a valid BIH entry; if it does not, you can buy insurance at the border. Ask your insurer before you travel.

q: How long does it take to cross the border at Izačić?
a: At the Izačić – Ličko Petrovo Selo border crossing you usually get through quickly outside the season, but there can be queues in summer and at weekends. It is busiest on Saturdays and Sundays in July and August. This crossing is the route to Plitvice, which is about 35 km from Bihać.

q: How do I pay for a taxi in Bihać?
a: Taxis in Bihać are usually paid in cash in marks, and some drivers also accept euros. Ask the price before the journey or ask for the meter to be switched on. You can order a taxi by phone, and your host can give you the number of a reliable driver. For longer journeys, for example to Plitvice, always agree the price in advance.

q: Is there public transport in Bihać?
a: Bihać has town and suburban bus services, but routes to villages along the Una and to Una National Park are infrequent. For trips to the Una, Plitvice or rafting, your own car or a taxi is the most practical option. For rafting with Una Olympic Rafting, ask us on +387 61 591 320 how best to reach the base in Grmuša.

q: What are the check-in and check-out times for apartments in Bihać?
a: Check-in is from 12:00, and check-out is by 11:00, or by 12:00 if nobody is arriving after you. You arrange your exact arrival time directly with the owner, so let them know roughly when you will arrive. If you are arriving late in the evening, mention it in your enquiry or send a message on WhatsApp to +387 61 591 320.

q: What if I arrive in Bihać on a Sunday when the shops are closed?
a: On Sundays you can buy basic groceries at petrol stations and bakeries, and restaurants and cafés are open as normal. The simplest option is to shop on Saturday or on the way in Croatia, where some shops open on Sundays. Also ask your host, who will often know what is open.
